exam.rules: Anyone getting a first Florida learner's license (age 15+) must pass the Class E Knowledge Exam: 50 multiple-choice questions on Florida traffic laws, safe driving practices and traffic signs/signals/markings, with no separately scored sign section. You need 40 correct (80%). The exam is given in English only. It can be taken at a driver license service center or tax collector office, through a school DELAP driver education course, or with an approved third-party provider; applicants under 18 may take it online with a third-party provider using a notarized Parent Proctoring Form, and anyone who passes through a third party can be randomly selected for a free re-test. Before applying, first-time applicants under 18 must complete the 6-hour Driver Education Traffic Safety (DETS) course; adults who have never been licensed complete the TLSAE course. You also need to pass vision and hearing screening, and minors need a parental consent form. The FLHSMV handbook lists a $10 fee for a written re-test.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to get a Florida learner's license?
questions.explain: Florida issues a Class E learner's license at age 15 at the earliest.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Requirements for Class E Learner's & Driver License'

questions.q: Who must ride with a driver who holds a Florida learner's license?
options: Nobody, once the learner has held the license for three months
A licensed driver age 21 or older in the closest seat to the right of the driver
Any licensed driver age 18 or older in any seat
A parent only, seated anywhere in the vehicle
questions.explain: A learner must always be accompanied by a licensed driver at least 21 years old sitting in the front seat closest to the right of the driver.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Important Info for Minor Drivers'

questions.q: During the first three months after a learner's license is issued, when may the learner drive?
questions.explain: For the first three months a learner may drive only in daylight; after that, until 10 p.m.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Restrictions for Minors (Driving Curfews)'

questions.q: After holding a learner's license for three months, until what time may a learner drive (with a 21+ licensed driver)?
questions.explain: After the first three months, learners may drive until 10 p.m., always with a licensed driver 21 or older.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Restrictions for Minors (Driving Curfews)'

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must be certified before a driver under 18 can get a Class E driver license?
questions.explain: A parent, guardian or responsible adult 21+ must certify at least 50 hours of driving experience, 10 of them at night.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Requirements for Class E Learner's & Driver License'

questions.q: A driver under 18 must hold a learner's license for how long before getting a Class E license?
options: 12 months or until turning 18, whichever comes first
questions.explain: Minors must hold the learner's license for 12 months or until their 18th birthday, whichever comes first.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Requirements for Class E Learner's & Driver License'

questions.q: A 16-year-old with a Class E license may NOT drive during which hours (unless driving to or from work or with a licensed driver 21+)?
questions.explain: Licensed 16-year-olds may drive only between 6 a.m. and 11 p.m. unless going to or from work or accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Restrictions for Minors (Driving Curfews)'

questions.q: A 17-year-old with a Class E license may NOT drive during which hours (unless driving to or from work or with a licensed driver 21+)?
questions.explain: Licensed 17-year-olds may not drive between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. unless going to or from work or accompanied by a licensed driver 21+.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Restrictions for Minors (Driving Curfews)'

questions.q: How many questions are on the Florida Class E Knowledge Exam, and how many must you answer correctly?
questions.explain: The Class E Knowledge Exam has 50 multiple-choice questions and you must get 40 right (80 percent).
questions.ref: FLHSMV, 'Class E Knowledge Exam & Driving Skills Test' web page (2026)

questions.q: Since August 1, 2025, what course must an applicant under 18 who has never held a license complete before applying for a learner's license?
options: The 6-hour Driver Education Traffic Safety (DETS) course
questions.explain: Under SB 994 (2025), first-time applicants under 18 must complete the 6-hour DETS course (or an approved school driver education course).
questions.ref: FLHSMV, 'Driver Education Traffic Safety (DETS)' web page (2026)

questions.q: An adult (18 or older) who has never held a driver license anywhere must complete which course before applying for a Florida license?
options: No course is required for adults
Traffic Law and Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE)
questions.explain: Anyone who has never held a license in any state or country must complete a TLSAE course; for under-18 applicants this is now the DETS course.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Traffic Law Substance Abuse Education (TLSAE) Course'

questions.q: A driver under 18 who accumulates 6 or more points within 12 months is automatically:
options: Required to retake the knowledge exam
Restricted to driving for business purposes only for one year
questions.explain: Minors with 6+ points in 12 months are restricted to 'Business Purposes Only' for one year; each extra point adds 90 days.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Mandatory Restriction for Minors'

questions.q: If a minor already under a 'business purposes only' restriction receives more points, the restriction is extended by:
options: Nothing; the restriction cannot be extended
questions.explain: The business-purposes restriction for minors is extended 90 days for every additional point received.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Mandatory Restriction for Minors'

questions.q: Under the Florida point system, 12 points within 12 months results in:
questions.explain: 12 points in 12 months = 30-day suspension; 18 in 18 months = 3 months; 24 in 36 months = 1 year.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Point System'

questions.q: How many points within 18 months lead to a 3-month suspension in Florida?
questions.explain: Accumulating 18 points within an 18-month period results in a 3-month suspension.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Point System'

questions.q: Accumulating 24 points within 36 months results in a suspension of:
questions.explain: 24 points within 36 months brings a one-year suspension.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Point System'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding 15 mph or less over the limit?
questions.explain: Unlawful speed of 15 mph or less over the limit carries 3 points; 16 mph or more over carries 4.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Common Violations and Associated Point Value'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding 16 mph or more over the posted limit (no crash)?
questions.explain: Speeding 16 mph or more over the limit is a 4-point violation; speeding that results in a crash is 6.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Common Violations and Associated Point Value'

questions.q: Passing a stopped school bus (with no injury) adds how many points to your record?
questions.explain: Passing a stopped school bus is 4 points, or 6 points if it causes serious injury or death.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Common Violations and Associated Point Value'

questions.q: Within how many days must you get a new license after changing your residential or mailing address?
questions.explain: Florida requires a new driver license within 30 calendar days of an address change.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Address and Name Changes'

questions.q: A non-resident who takes a job in Florida must obtain a Florida driver license within:
questions.explain: Non-residents who accept employment or enroll a child in public school must get a Florida license within 30 days to keep driving.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Who Needs a Florida License to Drive?'

questions.q: What vision standard meets Florida requirements without referral to an eye specialist?
options: 20/40 or better in each eye, with or without corrective lenses
questions.explain: 20/40 or better in each eye meets the standard; worse results lead to a referral.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Vision Screening'

questions.q: Restriction code 'B' on a Florida license means the driver must:
options: Wear corrective lenses at all times while driving
questions.explain: Code B is the corrective-lenses restriction; G is daylight only and 2 is ignition interlock.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Restriction Codes'

questions.q: Under Florida's No-Fault Law, what minimum coverage must vehicle owners carry?
options: $10,000 Personal Injury Protection and $10,000 Property Damage Liability
questions.explain: Owners must carry at least $10,000 PIP and $10,000 PDL and keep it continuously during registration.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'No-Fault Law'

questions.q: What can happen if you drive in Florida while knowing that your license is suspended?
options: You can be arrested and charged with a crime, with possible jail time and a fine
Nothing, as long as your vehicle is insured
You get only a written warning for a first offense
Nothing, if you are driving to or from work
questions.explain: Knowingly driving while suspended is a criminal offense: a misdemeanor that can bring jail time and a fine, with harsher penalties for repeat convictions (s. 322.34). An officer may take you to jail for it.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Financial Responsibility Law'

questions.q: To take the Class E Driving Skills Test, an applicant must have held a learner's license for 12 months or:
options: Have passed a second knowledge exam
Be 16 and a half years old
questions.explain: You qualify for the skills test after holding the learner's license 12 months or upon turning 18.
questions.ref: FLHSMV, 'Class E Knowledge Exam & Driving Skills Test' web page (2026)

questions.q: If a learner (under 18) is convicted of a moving violation, what happens to the required 12-month learner period?
options: The learner's license is permanently revoked
It is extended for one year from the conviction date or until age 18
It is shortened to six months
questions.explain: A moving violation conviction restarts the one-year holding period from the conviction date (or until 18, whichever comes first); one violation with adjudication withheld is allowed.
questions.ref: FLHSMV, 'Traffic Laws for Florida Teens' web page (2026); Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Requirements for Class E Learner's & Driver License'

questions.q: Who may take the Class E Knowledge Exam online through an approved third-party provider?
options: Anyone, regardless of age, with no parental form
questions.explain: Online knowledge exams through approved third parties are for applicants under 18 and require a Parent Proctoring Form.
questions.ref: FLHSMV, 'Class E Knowledge Exam & Driving Skills Test' web page (2026)

questions.q: If a basic driver improvement course is elected for a traffic ticket, how often may you make that election?
options: Not more than once in 12 months and no more than five times in a lifetime
questions.explain: You cannot elect a BDI course if you did so in the preceding 12 months, and you are limited to five elections in a lifetime.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Basic Driver Improvement (BDI) Course'

questions.q: Three convictions for reckless driving within one year will result in:
options: A requirement to retake the vision test
questions.explain: Florida law requires revocation for three reckless driving cases within one year.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Revocations'

questions.q: Which of the following is a Class E license NOT valid for?
options: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
questions.explain: Vehicles with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more require a commercial license; mopeds may be driven with a Class E license.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'License Classifications'

questions.q: At what blood or breath alcohol level is a driver 21 or older considered to be driving under the influence in Florida?
questions.explain: Your license is administratively suspended at arrest if your BAL is .08 or above.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Driving Under the Influence (DUI)'

questions.q: Under Florida's zero-tolerance law, a driver under 21 with a BAL of what level will have the license suspended?
questions.explain: Drivers under 21 with a BAL of .02 or more are automatically suspended for six months.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Zero Tolerance'

questions.q: How long is the license suspension for a first zero-tolerance violation (under 21, BAL .02 or more)?
questions.explain: A first zero-tolerance offense brings a six-month suspension; a second brings one year.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Zero Tolerance'

questions.q: A driver under 21 with a BAL of .05 or higher must also:
options: Take the driving skills test again
questions.explain: Under-21 drivers at .05 or higher must attend a substance abuse course in addition to the suspension.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Zero Tolerance'

questions.q: What alcohol level makes a commercial motor vehicle driver subject to commercial DUI penalties in Florida?
questions.explain: CMV drivers with any alcohol are put out of service for 24 hours, and at .04 or more they face commercial DUI penalties.
questions.ref: Florida Statutes s. 322.62 (commercial motor vehicle operators)

questions.q: Under Florida's Implied Consent Law, when did you agree to take a breath, blood or urine test if lawfully asked?
options: Only when you sign a form at the traffic stop
When you signed for your driver license
questions.explain: By signing your driver license you have agreed to submit to these tests when an officer has reasonable cause.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Implied Consent Law'

questions.q: What happens the first time you refuse a lawfully requested breath, urine or blood test?
options: Your license is suspended for one year
Nothing, if you are later found not guilty
Your license is suspended for 30 days
questions.explain: A first refusal brings a one-year license suspension. Since 2025 it is also a second-degree misdemeanor. A second refusal brings an 18-month suspension and a first-degree misdemeanor.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Implied Consent Law'

questions.q: A second refusal to submit to a lawful breath, urine or blood test results in:
options: An 18-month suspension and a first-degree misdemeanor
questions.explain: A second refusal means an 18-month suspension and a first-degree misdemeanor.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Implied Consent Law'

questions.q: In a DUI case involving death or serious injury, a blood test:
options: Can only be taken by a police officer
May be taken with or without your consent
Can only be taken with a signed consent form
questions.explain: In DUI cases with death or serious injury, blood must be drawn by a medical professional with or without consent, even if you are unconscious.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Implied Consent Law'

questions.q: What is the fine range for a first DUI conviction (BAL under .15, no minor in the vehicle)?
questions.explain: A first DUI carries a $500–$1,000 fine; with BAL .15+ or a minor in the vehicle it rises to $1,000–$2,000.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Penalties for DUI'

questions.q: How many hours of community service are required for a first DUI conviction?
questions.explain: A first DUI conviction includes 50 hours of community service.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Penalties for DUI'

questions.q: What is the minimum license revocation for a first DUI conviction?
questions.explain: Each listed DUI conviction level carries a minimum revocation of 180 days.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Penalties for DUI'

questions.q: For a first DUI conviction with a BAL of .15 or higher or a minor in the vehicle, the maximum jail term is:
questions.explain: Imprisonment is up to 6 months for a first DUI, or up to 9 months if BAL was .15+ or a minor was in the vehicle.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Penalties for DUI'

questions.q: How long must DUI school last for a first DUI conviction?
questions.explain: First-offense DUI school is 12 hours; second and third offenses require 21 hours.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Penalties for DUI'

questions.q: For a second DUI conviction, an ignition interlock device is required for at least:
questions.explain: A second conviction requires an ignition interlock device for at least one continuous year; a third requires two years.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Penalties for DUI'

questions.q: How long does a DUI conviction remain on your Florida driving record?
questions.explain: A DUI conviction must remain on your driving record for 75 years.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Drinking & Driving'

questions.q: Which ability is affected FIRST after drinking an alcoholic beverage?
questions.explain: Judgment is the first thing affected; reflexes, vision and coordination follow.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Drinking & Driving'

questions.q: Taking an allergy or cold medicine and then having one drink can:
options: Have the same effect as several drinks
Cancel out the effects of the alcohol
questions.explain: Mixing alcohol with drugs often multiplies their effects.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Drugged Driving'

questions.q: You can be charged with DUI in Florida if you are impaired by:
options: Alcohol, controlled substances, prescription drugs or over-the-counter medicines
Alcohol only when your BAL is above .15
questions.explain: DUI covers impairment from alcohol, controlled substances, prescriptions or over-the-counter medications.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Driving Under the Influence (DUI)'

questions.q: After a DUI arrest, within how many days must you request a review hearing to challenge the administrative suspension?
questions.explain: To appeal an administrative suspension you must apply to the Bureau of Administrative Reviews within 10 days of arrest.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Administrative Hearings'

questions.q: After a DUI conviction, what Bodily Injury Liability coverage must you carry for three years?
options: $100,000 per person / $300,000 per crash, plus $50,000 property damage
questions.explain: A DUI conviction requires 100/300 BIL and $50,000 PDL coverage for three years.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Financial Responsibility Law'

questions.q: Under Florida's open container law, which of these is illegal while a vehicle is being driven on a road?
options: A sealed six-pack on the back seat
An opened bottle stored in a locked glove compartment
A sealed bottle of wine in the trunk
A passenger in a car holding an opened can of beer
questions.explain: Drivers and passengers may not possess an open container in a moving car; an open container counts as the driver's unless a passenger holds it or it is locked away.
questions.ref: Florida Statutes s. 316.1936 (open containers)

questions.q: If you are convicted of possessing, selling or trafficking drugs, including marijuana, what happens to your driver license?
options: You must retake the vision test
It is only marked with a restriction code
questions.explain: Florida law requires license suspension for drug possession, sale or trafficking convictions.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Zero Tolerance'

questions.q: What is the fine range for a third DUI conviction (BAL under .15, no minor in the vehicle)?
questions.explain: A third DUI conviction carries a $2,000-$5,000 fine (at least $4,000 if BAL was .15+ or a minor was in the vehicle).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Penalties for DUI'

questions.q: If you are the designated driver for a group, how much alcohol should you drink?
questions.explain: A designated driver should not drink; even one drink is too many.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Drinking & Driving'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in a Florida municipal, business or residential area?
questions.explain: Florida's standard limit for municipal, business or residential areas is 30 mph unless posted otherwise.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Florida Standard Speed Limits'

questions.q: What is the standard speed limit in a Florida school zone?
questions.explain: School zones have a standard limit of 20 mph during the posted times or when lights flash.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Florida Standard Speed Limits'

questions.q: Unless another limit is posted, the maximum speed on Florida streets and highways (outside cities, not limited access) is:
questions.explain: Streets and highways have a 55 mph standard maximum except where otherwise posted.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Florida Standard Speed Limits'

questions.q: What is the maximum speed limit on Florida limited access highways?
questions.explain: Limited access highways have a 70 mph maximum, and no Florida speed limit is ever higher than 70.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Florida Standard Speed Limits'

questions.q: On a highway posted at 70 mph, what is the minimum speed limit?
questions.explain: Where the posted limit is 70 mph, the minimum speed is 50 mph.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Can you receive a citation in Florida for driving too slowly?
options: Yes, if you block or delay traffic moving at normal, safe speeds
questions.explain: Driving so slowly that you impede normal traffic is against Florida law.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: Is it legal to drive up to 10 mph over the limit in Florida?
options: Yes, when passing a slower car
No; any speed over the posted limit can be cited
Yes, there is a 10 mph buffer
questions.explain: The 'speeding buffer' is a myth; you may be cited for any speed over the limit.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: What is the minimum following distance recommended in the Florida handbook under good conditions?
questions.explain: Keep at least a four-second following distance in favorable conditions and more in bad weather or traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Following Distances'

questions.q: When should you increase your following distance beyond four seconds?
options: When following a motorcycle or driving on wet roads
When the car ahead is a small sedan
When the road is dry and traffic is light
Only when driving in a school zone
questions.explain: Increase following distance in rain, low visibility, when towing, behind motorcycles and behind vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Following Distances'

questions.q: How close may you legally follow a fire truck that is responding to an emergency?
questions.explain: It is against the law to follow a responding fire truck closer than 500 feet.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Following Distances'

questions.q: Outside business or residence districts, a truck or vehicle towing a trailer may not follow another truck or towing vehicle within:
questions.explain: Trucks and vehicles towing another vehicle must stay at least 300 feet behind another such vehicle, except when passing or in cities and towns.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Following Distance for Trucks'

questions.q: When you double your speed, your braking distance and force of impact become about:
questions.explain: Doubling speed makes braking distance and impact four times greater; tripling makes them nine times greater.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Braking Distance'

questions.q: When you triple your speed, the force of impact becomes about:
questions.explain: Tripling speed increases braking distance and impact about nine times.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Braking Distance'

questions.q: At 50 mph on dry pavement, about how far will you travel before stopping (perception, reaction and braking combined)?
questions.explain: Total stopping distance at 50 mph is at least 268 feet, nearly a football field.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Total Stopping Distance'

questions.q: Fines for speeding are doubled in which areas?
options: Active school zones and construction (work) zones
questions.explain: Speeding fines are doubled in school and construction zones.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Speeding'

questions.q: Under Florida's dangerous excessive speeding law (effective July 1, 2025), which of these counts as dangerous excessive speeding?
options: Driving 20 mph over the limit in a school zone
Driving 5 mph under the minimum speed
Driving 50 mph or more over the speed limit
questions.explain: It is dangerous excessive speeding to go 50+ mph over the limit, or 100+ mph in a way that threatens people or property.
questions.ref: Florida Statutes s. 316.1922 (dangerous excessive speeding, 2025)

questions.q: In bad weather, such as a heavy rainstorm, what speed should you drive?
options: Faster, to get out of the storm sooner
Slower than the posted limit, at a speed that keeps the car under full control
questions.explain: Speed limits apply to favorable conditions; you must adjust for weather, road and traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Speed Limits'

questions.q: On a two-lane road, a law enforcement car is stopped on the shoulder with lights flashing and the speed limit is 45 mph. What speed is required as you pass?
questions.explain: On a two-lane road you must slow to 20 mph below the posted limit when passing a stopped emergency or service vehicle.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: Under the Move Over Law, if the posted speed limit is 20 mph or less, what speed must you slow to?
options: You do not need to slow down
questions.explain: When the posted limit is 20 mph or less, you must slow to 5 mph.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: What does 'overdriving your headlights' mean?
options: Driving so fast that you cannot stop within the distance your headlights show
Using high beams in the city
questions.explain: At night, drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Night Driving'

questions.q: If a vehicle behind you is following too closely, the handbook advises you to:
options: Move into the left lane and stay there
Speed up to increase the gap
Brake suddenly to warn the driver
Slow down and keep to the right
questions.explain: When tailgated, slow down and keep right so the other driver can pass.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Following Distances'

questions.q: At an all-way stop, two vehicles arrive at about the same time. Who goes first?
questions.explain: Vehicles go in order of arrival; if they arrive together, each driver yields to the driver on the right.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Intersections'

questions.q: At an all-way stop, which vehicle should proceed first?
options: The first vehicle to reach the intersection
The vehicle on the busier road
questions.explain: At an all-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrived.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: At a two-way stop, one driver is turning and another is going straight. Who must yield?
questions.explain: At a two-way stop, the turning vehicle yields to the vehicle going straight.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Intersections'

questions.q: You are entering a paved road from an unpaved road at an open (uncontrolled) intersection. You must:
options: Go first because you are on the right
Yield to traffic on the paved road
Expect paved-road traffic to stop for you
questions.explain: At open intersections, a driver entering a paved road from an unpaved road must yield.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Open Intersections'

questions.q: At an open intersection, you are crossing a state highway from a secondary road. You must:
options: Yield the right-of-way to traffic on the state highway
Proceed first because the highway traffic must slow down
questions.explain: Drivers entering or crossing a state highway from a secondary road must yield at an open intersection.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Open Intersections'

questions.q: You want to turn left at an intersection and a car is approaching from the opposite direction. You should:
options: Turn only if you signal for 50 feet
Expect it to yield to you
questions.explain: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Open Intersections'

questions.q: When pulling out of a driveway or alley onto a road, you must:
options: Yield to vehicles on the road and to pedestrians and bicyclists on the sidewalk or in bike lanes
Proceed first because you were stopped
questions.explain: Drivers entering from a driveway, alley or roadside must yield to traffic already on the road and to people on the sidewalk.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Driveways'

questions.q: When leaving an alley, driveway or private road, what must you do before crossing a sidewalk?
options: Stop only if a crossing guard is present
Stop for pedestrians on the sidewalk
questions.explain: Drivers entering or leaving an alley, driveway or private road must stop for pedestrians on the sidewalk.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorists'

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights approaches from behind. What must you do?
options: Keep driving at the same speed in your lane
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Pull over to the closest edge of the roadway and stop until it passes
questions.explain: Pull to the nearest edge of the road, clear of intersections, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: A funeral procession is going through an intersection. What should you do?
options: Honk to let them know you are waiting
Follow the procession through the intersection
Yield and do not drive between vehicles in the procession
Cut in when your light turns green
questions.explain: Motorists must yield to funeral processions; once the lead vehicle enters, the rest may follow regardless of signals.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Funeral Processions'

questions.q: A public transit bus has signaled and is pulling out of a designated bus bay into your lane. You must:
options: Proceed because the bus must wait
Speed up to pass the bus
questions.explain: Drivers must yield to transit buses re-entering traffic from a designated pullout bay.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Public Transit'

questions.q: Who must yield when entering a roundabout?
options: Traffic in the roundabout yields to entering drivers
Whoever reaches the circle first from the left
The larger vehicle always has right-of-way
Drivers entering the roundabout yield to traffic already in it
questions.explain: Entering drivers yield to vehicles already circulating; if there is no traffic, you may enter without stopping.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: Traffic in a roundabout travels in which direction?
options: It depends on the time of day
questions.explain: Roundabouts operate one-way, counter-clockwise.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: When merging onto a limited access highway from an acceleration lane, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explain: Merging drivers must yield to traffic on the highway and merge only when safe.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Entering & Leaving Limited Access Highways'

questions.q: When may you stop in the acceleration lane while entering an expressway?
options: Whenever a truck is in the right lane
Whenever you want to check your mirrors
Only when traffic is too heavy and there is no space to merge safely
questions.explain: Do not stop in the acceleration lane unless traffic is too heavy and there is no space to enter safely.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Entering & Leaving Limited Access Highways'

questions.q: A pedestrian is using a white cane with a red tip at an intersection ahead. What must you do?
options: Proceed if you have a green light
Honk to let them know you are there
Come to a complete stop and yield
questions.explain: Come to a complete stop and yield to visually impaired pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorists'

questions.q: A car in the next lane is stopped at a crosswalk, and you cannot see why. You should:
options: Stop as well and assume a pedestrian may be crossing
questions.explain: You may not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian; assume someone is crossing even if you can't see them.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorists'

questions.q: If a pedestrian crosses a road at a point other than a crosswalk, who must yield?
options: The driver must always stop completely
The pedestrian must yield to vehicles, but drivers must still do everything possible to avoid hitting them
questions.explain: Pedestrians outside a crosswalk must yield, yet motorists must still do everything possible to avoid a collision.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Pedestrians'

questions.q: A traffic officer is directing traffic at an intersection with a working signal. Whom do you obey?
options: The car in front of you
Whichever is safer in your opinion
questions.explain: Signals must be obeyed except when an officer is directing traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: When a traffic signal is completely dark because of a power outage and no officer is present, treat the intersection as:
options: An open intersection with no rules
A green light for the main road
A yield to the right only
questions.explain: When signals are out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Power Outage'

questions.q: When turning right across a bike lane, you must:
options: Yield to any bicyclist and make the turn behind them
Stop in the bike lane and wait
Turn in front of the bicyclist quickly
questions.explain: Yield to bicyclists when crossing a bike lane to turn and turn behind them.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorists (Bicyclists)'

questions.q: When children or a school crossing guard are in a crosswalk, where must you stop?
options: In the middle of the crosswalk
You only need to slow down
At the stop line, not in the crosswalk
questions.explain: Yield and stop at the stop line, not in the crosswalk, when children or crossing guards are present.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'School Crossings'

questions.q: How far before a turn must you signal in Florida?
options: Just as you begin to turn
questions.explain: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turning'

questions.q: Which hand signal means a LEFT turn?
options: Right arm extended out the right window
questions.explain: Hand signals are given from the left side: straight out for left, up for right, down for slow or stop.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turning'

questions.q: Your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing UP. What does this signal mean?
questions.explain: Left forearm raised upward is the right-turn hand signal.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turning'

questions.q: Your left arm is extended and pointing DOWN. What does this signal mean?
questions.explain: Left arm pointing downward means slow or stop.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turning'

questions.q: Is it legal to use your turn signal to tell the driver behind you that it is safe to pass?
options: Yes, but only on two-lane roads
No, it is against the law
questions.explain: Using directional signals to tell drivers behind that they can pass is illegal in Florida.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turning'

questions.q: When turning right onto a multi-lane road, which lane should you turn into?
options: The right lane of the road you enter
questions.explain: Right turns should be completed into the right lane of the roadway entered.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turning'

questions.q: You reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are in the wrong lane. You should:
options: Turn from the wrong lane carefully
Back up to the correct position
Stop and wait for a gap to change lanes
Continue to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane
questions.explain: Never make last-minute turns; go on to the next intersection.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turning'

questions.q: When should you use a three-point turn?
options: On a curve where you can see well
Whenever you miss an exit on the highway
Only when the road is too narrow for a U-turn and you cannot go around the block
questions.explain: Use a three-point turn only on narrow roads when circling the block is not possible, never on curves, hills or highways.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Three-Point Turns'

questions.q: Where should you never make a three-point turn or U-turn?
questions.explain: Never turn around on a curve, a hill, a highway, or where a sign prohibits it.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Three-Point Turns'

questions.q: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: When the other driver flashes the lights
When you can see the tires of the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror
As soon as your front bumper clears its front bumper
questions.explain: Do not return until you can see the passed vehicle's tires in your rear-view mirror, and signal first.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing'

questions.q: When passing on a two-lane road, you must return to the right side before coming within how many feet of an approaching vehicle?
questions.explain: Return to the right side before you are within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing'

questions.q: You may not pass on a hill or curve unless you can see at least how far ahead?
questions.explain: Passing is prohibited on hills or curves where you cannot see at least 500 feet ahead.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing'

questions.q: Passing is not allowed within how many feet of an intersection, bridge, tunnel or railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Do not pass within 100 feet of an intersection, bridge, viaduct, tunnel or railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing'

questions.q: When is passing on the right legal in Florida?
options: When there are two or more lanes going your way, or the vehicle ahead is turning left
Whenever the left lane is busy
On any two-lane road if you use the shoulder
questions.explain: Passing on the right is legal only with two or more same-direction lanes or when the vehicle ahead is turning left.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing on the Right'

questions.q: May you exceed the speed limit while passing another vehicle?
options: Yes, if the pass is completed quickly
No, it is illegal to exceed the limit while passing
questions.explain: Stay within the speed limit; speeding while passing is illegal.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing'

questions.q: What should you do while another vehicle is passing you?
options: Move to the left side of your lane
Keep your speed and move to the right side of your lane
Speed up so the pass is shorter
questions.explain: Do not increase speed when being passed; move to the right to give room.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Being Passed'

questions.q: On a road with two or more lanes in your direction, you are in the far-left lane and a faster vehicle comes up behind you. Florida law requires you to:
options: Brake to slow the faster vehicle
Stay in the left lane at the speed limit
Move out of the left lane
questions.explain: Florida law requires drivers to move out of the left lane when being overtaken by a faster vehicle (unless passing or preparing to turn left).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing'; Florida Statutes s. 316.081(3) (left lane)

questions.q: On a two-lane highway (one lane each way), which lane must you drive in?
options: The right lane, except when passing where allowed
The lane closest to the center line
The left lane if it is smoother
questions.explain: On a two-lane highway always drive in the right lane unless overtaking and passing where permitted.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Traffic Lanes'

questions.q: The center lane of a three-lane or five-lane highway is used only for:
questions.explain: The center lane is reserved for left turns, not passing.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Traffic Lanes'

questions.q: In a multi-lane roundabout, which lane should you use to make a U-turn?
questions.explain: Use the left lane to go straight, turn left or make a U-turn; the right lane is for straight or right.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: When should you use your turn signal in a roundabout?
options: Only when changing lanes inside it
questions.explain: Signal before exiting; do not change lanes or stop inside a roundabout.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: You drive past your exit on a limited access highway. What should you do?
options: Stop and wait for traffic to clear
Make a U-turn through the median
questions.explain: If you miss your exit, go to the next one; never back up or cross the median.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'When Leaving a Limited Access Highway'

questions.q: After stopping at a red light, when may you turn left on red?
options: From any street when no cars are coming
Only from a two-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way street onto a one-way street with traffic moving to the left, if not prohibited and the way is clear
questions.explain: A left on red is allowed only from one-way onto one-way (leftward traffic) after stopping and yielding.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Steady Signal Lights'

questions.q: Before changing lanes, how should you check your blind spot?
options: Use only the inside rear-view mirror
Turn your head and look over your shoulder
Rely on the car's blind spot warning light
questions.explain: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors; turn your head to check them.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Blind Spots'

questions.q: What lane may you use on a highway marked with diamond symbols and HOV signs?
options: Vehicles with the required number of occupants (two or more) or approved low-emission vehicles
questions.explain: HOV lanes are reserved for vehicles with two or more occupants or decal-bearing low-emission vehicles; enter only at designated points.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'HOV Lanes'

questions.q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Florida?
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'It's Against the Law to Park'

questions.q: Parking is prohibited within how many feet of an intersection?
questions.explain: You may not park within 20 feet of an intersection.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'It's Against the Law to Park'

questions.q: How far must you park from a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'It's Against the Law to Park'

questions.q: Parking is prohibited within how many feet of a stop sign, flashing signal or traffic signal?
questions.explain: Do not park within 30 feet of any flashing signal, stop sign or traffic signal.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'It's Against the Law to Park'

questions.q: How close may you park to the entrance of a fire, ambulance or rescue station?
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited within 20 feet of the entrance to a fire, ambulance or rescue station.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'It's Against the Law to Park'

questions.q: When parallel parking, your right-hand wheels must be within how many inches of the curb?
questions.explain: Park parallel to the curb with your right wheels within 12 inches of the curb or side of the road.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Parking'

questions.q: When parking DOWNHILL next to a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
questions.explain: Downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb so the car would roll into it.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Parking on Hills'

questions.q: When parking UPHILL next to a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: Toward the center line only if there is no traffic
questions.explain: Uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the tire rests against it if the car rolls back.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Parking on Hills'

questions.q: When parking UPHILL on a road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: Toward the center of the road
questions.explain: Uphill without a curb, turn the wheels to the right so the car would roll off the road, away from traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Parking on Hills'

questions.q: What does Florida law require you to do with your keys before leaving your parked vehicle?
options: Leave them in the ignition for emergencies
questions.explain: Florida law requires that you take the keys out of your vehicle before leaving it.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Parking'

questions.q: Which of these is a legal place to park, assuming no signs or markings prohibit it?
options: Along a curb 25 feet from an intersection
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited on bridges, in bike lanes and by yellow curbs; 25 feet from an intersection exceeds the 20-foot rule.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'It's Against the Law to Park'

questions.q: Who may park in a space marked with this sign?
options: Anyone parking for less than 15 minutes
Any vehicle with hazard lights on
A vehicle displaying a disabled parking permit or plate that is transporting the permit holder
questions.explain: The vehicle must display the permit and actually be transporting the person with the disability.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Disabled Parking Permit Violations'

questions.q: If your vehicle breaks down on a limited access highway and you move it onto the shoulder, how long may it remain there?
questions.explain: A disabled vehicle may stay on the shoulder of a limited access highway for no more than six hours.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Limited Access Highway Safety Reminders'

questions.q: On a two-way street, on which side should you park?
options: The left side, facing oncoming traffic
The right side, facing the direction of traffic
questions.explain: Always park on the right side of the road (unless it's a one-way street), parallel to the curb in the direction of traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Parking'

questions.q: What is the minimum clearance Florida law requires when passing a bicyclist?
questions.explain: Give bicyclists at least three feet of clearance when passing.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorists (Bicyclists)'

questions.q: On a two-lane road with a double yellow center line, may you briefly cross the center line to pass a bicyclist?
options: Only if the bicyclist waves you by
Yes, when it is safe to do so
questions.explain: Florida allows crossing a double solid yellow line to pass a bicyclist when it is safe.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: Under Florida law, a bicycle is legally considered:
options: A vehicle only when it has a motor
A vehicle with the same rights and duties as other drivers
A toy that must stay on sidewalks
questions.explain: A bicycle is a vehicle with the privileges and responsibilities of motor vehicle drivers (except on limited access highways).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Bicyclists and passengers under what age must wear a helmet in Florida?
questions.explain: All bicycle riders and passengers under 16 must wear a helmet meeting federal standards.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Bicyclists'

questions.q: At night, what lighting must a bicycle have?
options: A white front light visible from 500 feet and a red rear reflector and red light visible from 600 feet
A red front light and white rear light
No lights if the rider wears reflective clothing
questions.explain: Between sunset and sunrise, bicycles need a front white light (500 ft) and rear red reflector plus red light (600 ft).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Bicyclists'

questions.q: When may a bicyclist use the full travel lane?
options: Never; bicycles must always ride on the shoulder
When the lane is too narrow for a car and bike to share safely, or to turn left or avoid hazards
questions.explain: Cyclists may take the full lane when it is too narrow to share, when passing, turning left or avoiding hazards.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Bicyclists'

questions.q: Before opening your car door after parallel parking, you should:
options: Check for approaching bicyclists and traffic
questions.explain: Always check for cyclists and vehicles before opening a door into traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorists (Bicyclists)'

questions.q: May a car share a lane side-by-side with a motorcycle?
options: No, the motorcyclist is entitled to the full lane
Yes, if the lane is wide
questions.explain: Do not share a lane with a motorcycle; it is entitled to the entire lane.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Motorcycles and Mopeds'

questions.q: Why is it hard to judge the speed and distance of an approaching motorcycle?
options: Motorcycles do not have brake lights
Its small size makes it seem farther away than it is
Motorcycle headlights are dimmer by law
Motorcycles always travel faster than cars
questions.explain: Motorcycles take up less of your field of vision, so they may seem farther away than they really are.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Motorcycles and Mopeds'

questions.q: Why may a motorcycle slow down without showing a brake light?
options: Riders often slow by downshifting or rolling off the throttle
Brake lights are illegal on motorcycles in Florida
Motorcycles do not have brake lights
questions.explain: Motorcyclists often slow by downshifting or easing off the throttle, which does not activate the brake light.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Motorcycles and Mopeds'

questions.q: Who may ride a motorcycle in Florida without a helmet?
options: A rider 21 or older who carries at least $10,000 in medical insurance
Any rider on roads under 35 mph
questions.explain: Motorcycle operators must wear a helmet unless they are 21+ AND carry a $10,000 medical benefits policy.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorcycle/Moped Riders'

questions.q: What license do you need to operate a moped in Florida?
options: A Class E driver license (no motorcycle endorsement needed)
questions.explain: Moped operators must have a Class E license; a motorcycle endorsement is not required.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorcycle/Moped Riders'

questions.q: The 'No Zone' around a large truck refers to:
options: Lanes where trucks may not drive
The blind spots in front, behind and on both sides where the driver can't see you
The area where trucks may not park
questions.explain: No Zones are the large blind spots around a commercial vehicle; stay out of them.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: After passing a large truck, when is it safe to move back in front of it?
options: Immediately after your rear bumper clears its front
When you can see the truck's cab in your rear-view mirror
questions.explain: Don't cut in too soon; trucks can't stop quickly. Wait until the cab is visible in your rear-view mirror.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing Commercial Vehicles'

questions.q: A large truck ahead is signaling a right turn and swinging wide to the left. You should:
options: Pass on the right before it turns
Stay back and not drive between the truck and the curb
Honk and pass on the left
questions.explain: Trucks often swing left to make right turns; never squeeze between the truck and the curb.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: Why should you avoid passing a large truck on a downgrade?
options: It is illegal to pass any vehicle downhill
Its weight and momentum will make it speed up
Trucks cannot use their brakes downhill
Trucks always slow down on hills
questions.explain: A truck's weight and momentum cause it to gain speed going downhill.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing Commercial Vehicles'

questions.q: You are stopped behind a large truck on an upgrade. What should you do?
options: Honk so the driver knows you are there
Stay directly behind the center of the trailer
Leave extra space in case it rolls back, and stay to the left in your lane so the driver can see you
questions.explain: Trucks may drift back when starting on a hill; leave room and keep left in your lane to be seen.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: On a two-way road, a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop arm out. Which drivers must stop?
options: Only drivers in the lane next to the bus
questions.explain: On a two-way street or highway, traffic moving in either direction must stop for a stopped school bus.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: On a divided highway with a raised median or an unpaved median at least 5 feet wide, a school bus stops on the other side. You:
options: Must stop only if children are visible
Do not have to stop, but should proceed with caution
Must stop until the stop arm is withdrawn
questions.explain: Traffic in the opposite direction need not stop when a raised barrier or unpaved median of at least 5 feet separates them from the bus.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: A school bus stops on a multi-lane road where the lanes are separated only by a painted median. Traffic in the opposite direction must:
options: Move to the far left lane and continue
questions.explain: Painted lines or pavement markings are not considered barriers, so traffic in both directions must stop.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: How long must you remain stopped for a school bus displaying its stop signal?
options: Until the stop signal is withdrawn and all children are clear of the road
Until the children are on the sidewalk, even if the stop arm is out
questions.explain: Remain stopped until the bus withdraws its stop signal and the children have cleared the roadway.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'School Buses'

questions.q: When a bicyclist rides on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk, the bicyclist must:
options: Ring a bell only at night
Ride in the street whenever pedestrians are present
Yield to pedestrians and give an audible signal before passing them
questions.explain: On sidewalks and crosswalks, cyclists have pedestrian rights and duties but must yield to pedestrians and signal audibly before passing.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Bicyclists'

questions.q: Under Florida's Move Over Law, what must you do on a multi-lane road when you approach a stopped tow truck with flashing lights on the shoulder?
options: Move out of the lane closest to it when safe, or slow to 20 mph below the limit if you can't
Nothing; the law covers only police vehicles
questions.explain: Vacate the lane nearest the stopped vehicle; if you can't safely, slow to 20 mph below the posted limit.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: Which of these is protected by Florida's Move Over Law (as expanded in 2024)?
options: A moving garbage truck in traffic
A disabled car stopped on the shoulder with its hazard lights on
A car parked legally in a driveway
A bus driving in the right lane
questions.explain: The Move Over Law also covers disabled vehicles displaying hazard lights, using flares/signage, or with people visibly present.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: Farm vehicles that must display this emblem on the rear are designed to operate at speeds below:
questions.explain: The SMV emblem is required on vehicles designed to operate under 25 mph.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Slow Moving Vehicles'

questions.q: A person under 18 may drive a golf cart on a public road designated for golf carts only if they:
options: Hold a valid learner's license or driver license
questions.explain: Since October 2023, golf cart operators under 18 on public roads must have a learner's license or driver license.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Golf Carts'

questions.q: Low-speed vehicles (LSVs) may be operated only on streets with a posted speed limit of:
questions.explain: LSVs, which have top speeds of 21–25 mph, are restricted to streets posted 35 mph or less.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Low-Speed Vehicles'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT allowed on Florida limited access highways?
questions.explain: Pedestrians, bicycles, animal-drawn vehicles and motor scooters of 150 cc or less are not allowed on limited access highways.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Limited Access Highways'

questions.q: Where should a pedestrian walk on a road with no sidewalk?
options: In the middle of the lane
On the left shoulder, facing traffic
On the right shoulder, with traffic
Either side, with their back to traffic
questions.explain: Pedestrians without a sidewalk should walk on the left side shoulder, facing oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Pedestrians'

questions.q: How much following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle?
questions.explain: Keep more than a four-second buffer behind motorcycles and increase it in bad weather or rough road conditions.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Motorcycles and Mopeds'

questions.q: When following a large truck at night, you should:
options: Use high beams so the driver sees you
questions.explain: High beams reflect off a truck's large mirrors and blind the driver.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Commercial Motor Vehicles'

questions.q: What are the three main categories of driver distraction?
questions.explain: Distractions are visual (eyes off road), manual (hands off wheel) and cognitive (mind off driving).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Distracted Driving'

questions.q: Why is texting one of the most dangerous driving distractions?
options: It involves all three types of distraction: visual, manual and cognitive
It is only a manual distraction
Phones interfere with the car's electronics
questions.explain: Texting takes your eyes, hands and mind off driving at once.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Distracted Driving'

questions.q: In which places does Florida law ban using a wireless device in a handheld manner while driving, even for calls?
options: School zones, school crossings and active work zones
questions.explain: Florida prohibits handheld use of a wireless device in designated school crossings, school zones and work zones; texting while driving is illegal everywhere.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Distracted Driving'

questions.q: In Florida, is texting while driving (a moving vehicle) legal?
options: No, it is illegal and officers may stop you for it
Yes, if done with one hand
Yes, if the speed is under 25 mph
questions.explain: Florida's Ban on Texting While Driving Law makes texting while operating a vehicle a primary offense.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Distracted Driving'; Florida Statutes s. 316.305 (texting ban)

questions.q: A texting-while-driving conviction that counts as a moving violation (a second offense within 5 years) adds how many points to your record?
questions.explain: The handbook lists texting while driving as 3 points. Under s. 316.305 a first offense is a nonmoving violation; a repeat offense within 5 years is a moving violation and carries 3 points. Unlawful wireless device use that causes a crash carries 6 points.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Common Violations and Associated Point Value'

questions.q: Under Florida law, who must wear a safety belt in a passenger car?
options: The driver, all front-seat passengers and all passengers under 18
questions.explain: Drivers, front-seat passengers and every passenger under 18 must be buckled.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Safety Belts and Child Passenger Safety'

questions.q: A 16-year-old passenger in the back seat is not wearing a seat belt. Who gets the ticket?
options: The vehicle's owner if not present
questions.explain: Drivers are charged when any passenger under 18 is not properly restrained.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Safety Belts and Child Passenger Safety'

questions.q: A 19-year-old front-seat passenger is not wearing a seat belt. Who is charged?
questions.explain: Passengers 18 or older are charged themselves for not wearing a required safety belt.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Safety Belts and Child Passenger Safety'

questions.q: Under Florida law, children under what age must ride in a separate carrier or integrated child safety seat?
questions.explain: Children through age 3 must be in a safety seat; ages 4 and 5 may use a safety seat or booster seat.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Safety Belts and Child Passenger Safety'; Florida Statutes s. 316.613 (child restraints)

questions.q: What must a 5-year-old ride in, under Florida law, when transported by a parent?
options: Nothing special if in the back seat
A child safety seat or a booster seat
questions.explain: Ages 4 and 5 must use a safety seat or booster seat.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Safety Belts and Child Passenger Safety'

questions.q: Where does the handbook recommend children under 13 ride?
options: In any seat with an airbag
questions.explain: Children under 13 should sit in the back because airbags can injure or kill young children.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Child Passenger Safety Seats/Restraints'

questions.q: Between what hours must you use your headlights in Florida?
options: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
questions.explain: Florida law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise, and when visibility is reduced.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Night Driving'

questions.q: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you switch from high beams to low beams?
questions.explain: Dim your high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Night Driving'

questions.q: Within how many feet of a vehicle you are following must you use low beams?
questions.explain: Do not use high beams within 300 feet of the vehicle ahead.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Night Driving'

questions.q: In Florida, when you turn on your windshield wipers because of rain, you must also:
questions.explain: Florida law requires headlights whenever your wipers are on due to weather.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rain'

questions.q: When driving in fog, smoke or heavy rain, which lights should you use?
questions.explain: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility; use low beams. Parking lights are not a substitute.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Low Visibility'

questions.q: High beam headlights reveal objects up to about:
questions.explain: High beams show objects about 450 feet ahead; low beams about 150 feet.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Night Driving'

questions.q: If an oncoming vehicle's headlights are blinding you at night, you should:
options: Look toward the right edge of the road and use lane lines as a guide
Stare at the headlights to judge distance
questions.explain: Avoid looking directly at oncoming lights; use lane lines as guides and glance at the other vehicle's position.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Night Driving'

questions.q: On long trips, how often does the handbook recommend taking a break to avoid drowsy driving?
questions.explain: Take a break every 100 miles or 2 hours on long trips.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Drowsy Driving'

questions.q: If another driver is threatening you or driving aggressively around you, you should:
options: Brake suddenly to teach them a lesson
Make eye contact to show you're not afraid
Stay calm, slow down to let them pass and avoid eye contact
questions.explain: Put distance between you and the aggressive driver, avoid eye contact and call *FHP (*347) or 911 if needed.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Road Rage'

questions.q: What number can you dial on a cell phone to reach the Florida Highway Patrol?
questions.explain: *FHP (*347) connects you to the Florida Highway Patrol.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Road Rage'

questions.q: Where do more crashes happen than any other place?
questions.explain: Use extra caution at intersections; more crashes happen there than anywhere else.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Defensive Driving'

questions.q: If a crash is unavoidable, which choice does the handbook say is better?
options: Hitting an oncoming vehicle head-on rather than a tree
Swerving off the road rather than into oncoming traffic
Skidding off the road rather than driving off it
Hitting a solid post rather than a hedge
questions.explain: It is better to drive off the road than into oncoming traffic, and better to hit something soft or stationary.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Defensive Driving'

questions.q: An animal suddenly runs in front of your car and a collision can't be avoided. What should you do?
options: Brake firmly and stay in your lane rather than swerve
questions.explain: Do not swerve into traffic or off the road; that can cause a more serious crash.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Animals'

questions.q: When are animals, such as deer, most active near roads?
questions.explain: Use caution at dawn and dusk; deer crashes are most common from October to December.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Animals'

questions.q: What is hydroplaning?
options: Your tires riding on a layer of water instead of the road
questions.explain: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the road on a film of water; worn tires, low pressure and speed increase the risk.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rain'

questions.q: When are roads often most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: After it has rained for several hours
When it first starts to rain after a dry period
questions.explain: Roads are especially slick when it hasn't rained in a while because oil builds up on the surface.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rain'

questions.q: You come to a road covered by floodwater. What should you do?
options: Turn around and find another route
Follow the car ahead through the water
Drive through slowly in low gear
questions.explain: You can't judge the depth or current; your vehicle could be swept away.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rain'

questions.q: What is the safest way to back up a vehicle?
options: Turn and look directly through the rear window, and back slowly
Back quickly to limit time in traffic
questions.explain: Look over your shoulder through the rear window; don't rely solely on mirrors or cameras.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Backing Up'

questions.q: What minimum tire tread depth does the handbook state?
questions.explain: Tires should have at least 3/32 inch of tread with no worn spots showing the ply.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Equipment Standards'

questions.q: What should you do when pulled over by a law enforcement officer?
options: Keep the engine running and the radio on
Search for your documents before the officer arrives
Stay in the car with your hands visible, such as on the steering wheel
Get out and walk toward the officer
questions.explain: Pull over safely, turn off the engine, stay inside and keep your hands visible; at night turn on the interior light.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Interacting with Law Enforcement'

questions.q: Are airbags a substitute for safety belts?
options: No; airbags are designed to work together with safety belts
questions.explain: Airbags are NOT a replacement for wearing a safety belt.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Air Bags'

questions.q: In an emergency stop in a car with anti-lock brakes (ABS), you should:
options: Press hard on the brake, hold it and steer
questions.explain: With ABS, keep firm, steady pressure and steer; pumping turns the ABS off.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Emergency Braking'

questions.q: In an emergency stop where traction is lost in a car with conventional (non-ABS) brakes, you should:
options: Press and hold the brake as hard as possible
questions.explain: Drivers with conventional brakes should pump the brakes when traction is lost.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Emergency Braking'

questions.q: Red reflectors on the lane lines are facing you. What does this mean?
options: You are approaching a toll plaza
You are driving the wrong way and must turn around or change lanes immediately
questions.explain: Red reflectors facing you mean you are on the wrong side of the road.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Red Reflectors on Lane Lines'

questions.q: What is the greatest danger on limited access highways?
options: Rear-end collisions from following too closely
questions.explain: Rear-end crashes are the greatest danger on limited access highways; don't follow too closely.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Limited Access Highway Safety Reminders'

questions.q: In Florida, interstate exit numbers are based on:
options: The order of exits from the state line (1, 2, 3...)
The distance to the next city
questions.explain: Florida exits match the mile markers on the highway.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Limited Access Highway Safety Reminders'

questions.q: You are in a minor crash with no injuries and your car is blocking traffic. You must:
options: Leave the scene and report it later
Move the vehicle out of traffic or have it moved
Leave it in place until police arrive
questions.explain: If the crash is minor and your vehicle blocks traffic, you must move it or have it moved.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Your Responsibilities After a Crash'

questions.q: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?
options: Leave a note with your name, contact information and license plate number, and notify law enforcement
Drive away since no one saw it
Report it only to your insurance company
