questions.explain: Try to locate the owner and notify police; if you can't, leave a note with your name, contact info and plate number.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Your Responsibilities After a Crash'

questions.q: If a crash causes property damage but no police report is required, within how many days must you send a written report to FLHSMV?
questions.explain: If no law enforcement report is made, you must file a written report with FLHSMV within 10 days.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Your Responsibilities After a Crash'

questions.q: Leaving the scene of a crash that results in a death is a:
options: First-degree felony with a minimum 4-year prison term
questions.explain: Hit-and-run causing death is a first-degree felony with a minimum four-year sentence and at least a 3-year license loss.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Hit and Run Penalties'

questions.q: For how long will you lose your license for leaving the scene of a crash involving injury or death?
questions.explain: Hit-and-run penalties involving injury or death include losing your license for at least three years.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Hit and Run Penalties'

questions.q: How should you treat an injured person who may be in shock?
options: Sit them upright and remove their jacket
Keep them calm and warm, have them lie flat with legs raised, and give nothing to drink
Leave them alone until they feel better
Give them water and have them walk around
questions.explain: Treat for shock: keep calm, lie flat with legs elevated, cover with a blanket, keep the airway open, nothing to drink.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Treat for Shock'

questions.q: An injured motorcyclist is lying in the road wearing a helmet. You should:
options: Leave the helmet on and call for help
Move the rider to the shoulder immediately
questions.explain: Do not remove an injured rider's helmet or move someone who may have a neck or spinal injury.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'First Aid'

questions.q: Your car breaks down on the highway. Which of these should you do?
options: Turn off all lights to save the battery
Have passengers get out on the traffic side
Leave it in the lane and walk for help
Get all four wheels out of the travel lanes and turn on your hazard lights
questions.explain: Move the vehicle completely out of traffic, turn on hazards, and have passengers exit on the side away from traffic.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Breakdowns/Disabled Vehicles'

questions.q: If possible, where should you stop a disabled vehicle so it can be seen?
options: In the middle of a bridge
Just over the crest of a hill
Where it can be seen for 200 feet in each direction
questions.explain: Park the disabled vehicle where it is visible for 200 feet each way.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Breakdowns/Disabled Vehicles'

questions.q: Your car begins to skid on a wet road. What should you do first?
options: Take your foot off the gas and steer in the direction you want to go
Turn the wheel sharply the opposite way
questions.explain: Ease off the gas, avoid braking if possible, and steer where you want the front of the car to go.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Skidding/Hydroplaning'

questions.q: Your right wheels drift off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?
options: Jerk the steering wheel left immediately
Speed up to get back on the pavement
Ease off the gas, hold the wheel firmly, brake lightly, and return to the road slowly when clear
questions.explain: Steer straight, slow gently and return to the pavement at low speed when it's clear.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Right Wheels Off Pavement'

questions.q: A tire suddenly blows out. What should you do?
options: Take your foot off the gas, hold the steering steady, and slow gradually
questions.explain: Don't brake hard; concentrate on steering, slow gradually, then brake softly and pull off the road.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Tire Blowout'

questions.q: Your gas pedal sticks. What should you do?
options: Shift into neutral (automatic) or press the clutch (manual), brake gently and steer to safety
questions.explain: Shift to neutral first; shutting off the engine can cause loss of steering control.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Jammed Gas Pedal'

questions.q: Your car stalls on railroad tracks and a train is coming. What should you do?
options: Run straight down the tracks away from the train
Stay in the car and try to restart it
Get everyone out and move away at an angle toward the train
Push the car off the tracks
questions.explain: Get out immediately and run at a 45-degree angle away from the tracks in the direction of the train to avoid debris.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Stalled on Railroad Tracks'

questions.q: What should you do if you see a train approaching a crossing that has no gates or lights?
options: Cross if the train seems far away
Stop and wait until the train has passed
questions.explain: Trains are faster than they look and can't stop quickly; stop and let it pass.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Railroad Crossing Signs & Signals'

questions.q: Your car goes into a canal and starts to sink. What should you do first?
options: Wait for the car to fill with water
Unbuckle and try to get out through a window before the car sinks
Call 911 before trying to get out
questions.explain: A car floats only 30–60 seconds; unbuckle, roll down a window and get out. Call 911 after you are out.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Submerged Vehicle'

questions.q: Your vehicle catches fire. Which action is correct?
options: Open the hood fully to fight the fire
Get out of the vehicle and call 911
Stay inside to stay safe from fumes
Pour water on a gasoline fire
questions.explain: Exit the vehicle and call for help; never apply water to a gasoline or diesel fire.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Fire'

questions.q: A vehicle is coming toward you in your lane. What should you do?
options: Sound the horn, flash your lights, brake and steer toward the side of the road
Stop in your lane and wait
questions.explain: Warn the driver, brake hard and steer to the side of the road (not into the oncoming lane).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Vehicle Approaching in Your Lane'

questions.q: After driving through deep water, your brakes feel weak. What should you do?
options: Drive fast to dry them with air
Stop and wait for an hour
Drive slowly in a low gear and apply the brakes lightly to dry them
questions.explain: Test brakes lightly and dry them by driving slowly in low gear while applying the brakes.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Wet Brakes'

questions.q: What is the blue Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign found at railroad crossings used for?
options: Contacting the railroad if there is a problem or something on the tracks
questions.explain: Every highway-rail crossing has a blue ENS sign with emergency contact information for the railroad.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Stalled on Railroad Tracks'

questions.q: If your steering wheel is pulling you off the road and you begin to overcorrect, the handbook advises you to:
options: Stay calm, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas and steer where you want to go
Turn the wheel sharply and slam the brakes
questions.explain: Overcorrecting can cause rollovers or a crash into oncoming traffic; stay calm and steer smoothly.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Overcorrection'

questions.q: If you come upon a crash scene, the handbook advises you to:
options: Call 911 or *FHP even if you think someone else already called
Stop in the travel lane to help
questions.explain: Don't assume someone else has called; pull well off the road and use hazards.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'First Aid'

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Yield to traffic on your left only
Come to a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk or intersection
Slow down and proceed if clear
Stop only if other cars are present
questions.explain: A stop sign requires a full stop at the stop line, or before the crosswalk or intersection if there is no line.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Always come to a complete stop
Slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic crossing your path; stop if necessary
questions.explain: Yield means slow down and let crossing vehicles go; if clear, you may proceed slowly without stopping.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not enter this road from your direction
questions.explain: Do Not Enter is posted on one-way roads and ramps you may not enter.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: You see this sign facing you. What should you do?
options: Speed up to exit the road
Pull onto the shoulder and wait
Turn around immediately; you are going against traffic
questions.explain: A Wrong Way sign means you are traveling in the wrong direction and must turn around right away.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: This sign appears below a stop sign. What does it tell you?
options: Traffic from all directions must stop
You may turn right without stopping
questions.explain: An All Way plaque means every approach has a stop sign; go in order of arrival.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The maximum legal speed under good conditions is 55 mph
The recommended speed for a curve is 55 mph
questions.explain: Speed limit signs show the fastest you may legally drive under favorable conditions.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign prohibit?
questions.explain: A red circle and slash over a left arrow means no left turn at this location.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: U-turns are allowed only on green
You may not turn around to go in the opposite direction
questions.explain: The No U-Turn sign prohibits turning around at this location.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: At an intersection with this sign and a red light, what may you do?
options: Wait for a green signal before turning
questions.explain: No Turn on Red means you may not turn right or left while the light is red.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Traffic may travel only in the direction of the arrow
Turn in the direction of the arrow immediately
questions.explain: One Way signs mean traffic flows only in the arrow's direction.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not pass other vehicles here
questions.explain: Do Not Pass signs mark areas where passing is prohibited.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell drivers?
options: Slow vehicles must use the left lane
Drivers in the left lane should move right unless they are passing
questions.explain: Slower traffic must stay right except to pass and must leave the left lane when overtaken.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: This sign is over a lane. What does it mean for drivers in that lane?
options: They must turn in the direction of the arrow
Only buses may use the lane
They may go straight or turn
questions.explain: A lane marked with a turn arrow and ONLY requires you to turn that way.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Turn Lanes'

questions.q: When this sign is posted with a green signal, what must you do before turning left?
options: Stop until the light turns yellow
Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
Turn immediately; you have the right-of-way
questions.explain: On a green ball, left turns are allowed but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Steady Signal Lights'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: The crossbuck is a yield sign for trains; a plaque below shows the number of tracks if more than one.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Railroad Crossing Signs & Signals'

questions.q: This round yellow sign is usually the first sign you see when approaching what?
questions.explain: The round advance warning sign tells you a highway-rail crossing is ahead.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Railroad Crossing Signs & Signals'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: The road curves to the right; slow down and don't pass
questions.explain: A curve sign warns of a right curve ahead; slow and don't pass.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: A cross road intersects the highway ahead
questions.explain: A cross road sign warns of an intersection; watch for traffic from left and right.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The right lane ends ahead; traffic must merge left
questions.explain: Reduction of lanes: right-lane traffic merges left and left-lane drivers should let them in.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The divided highway ends; you will soon be on a road with two-way traffic
questions.explain: Divided Highway Ends signs warn of two-way traffic 350–500 feet ahead; keep right.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: There is a stop sign ahead; be ready to stop
questions.explain: Stop Ahead warns that a stop sign is coming up.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Speed up to get through quickly
Drive slowly in wet weather and avoid quick braking or acceleration
questions.explain: Slippery When Wet: slow down, don't brake or speed up suddenly, and turn at low speed.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Watch for people crossing and be ready to slow or stop
Speed up to clear the area
Stop every time you see the sign
questions.explain: Pedestrian Crossing: slow down or stop to yield to pedestrians.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What does this five-sided sign tell you?
options: You are near a school; watch for children
questions.explain: The pentagon-shaped school sign means you are near a school; watch for children at all times.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'School Zone Signs & Signals'

questions.q: This yellow pennant-shaped sign on the left side of the road means:
questions.explain: The pennant marks the beginning of a no-passing zone.
questions.ref: MUTCD sign W14-3; Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Passing'

questions.q: This sign is posted below a curve warning sign. What does it mean?
options: The legal minimum speed is 35 mph
Trucks only must slow to 35 mph
The speed limit after the curve is 35 mph
The recommended maximum safe speed for the curve is 35 mph
questions.explain: Advisory speed signs show the fastest safe speed for the hazard ahead and may be used with any warning sign.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: What do orange signs like this one indicate?
questions.explain: Orange signs warn of construction and maintenance work zones, where speeding fines are doubled.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Traffic Sign Colors'

questions.q: What does a steady red signal like this require?
options: Stop at the stop line and remain stopped until green, except for a permitted turn on red
Speed up to clear the intersection
Stop only if traffic is coming
questions.explain: On red, stop completely; a right turn (or left from one-way to one-way) is allowed after stopping if not prohibited.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Steady Signal Lights'

questions.q: What does a steady yellow signal like this mean?
options: The light is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely
Stop only if a police officer is present
Proceed with caution; the light will stay yellow
Speed up to beat the red light
questions.explain: A steady yellow warns the light is changing to red; stop if it is safe.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Steady Signal Lights'

questions.q: The signal is green like this. What must you still do?
options: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection
questions.explain: Green means go only if the intersection is clear; yield to pedestrians and vehicles in it.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Steady Signal Lights'

questions.q: A green arrow pointing left like this means:
options: You may turn left in the direction of the arrow, yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection
You must yield to all oncoming traffic before turning
questions.explain: A green arrow allows the turn shown; still yield to anyone already in the intersection.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Steady Signal Lights'

questions.q: What should you do at a flashing red signal like this?
options: Treat it like a stop sign: stop, then proceed when safe
Slow down and proceed without stopping
Wait for the light to turn green
questions.explain: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Flashing Signal Lights'

questions.q: What does a flashing yellow signal like this mean?
options: The light is about to turn red
questions.explain: A flashing yellow warns of a hazard or dangerous intersection; slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Flashing Signal Lights'

questions.q: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns means:
options: You may turn left but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
You have a protected left turn
You must stop and wait for green
questions.explain: A flashing yellow arrow permits turning after yielding, since oncoming traffic has a green light.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Flashing Signal Lights'

questions.q: What do these pavement markings in the center of the road mean?
options: This is a center left-turn lane
Lanes moving in the same direction
Passing is not allowed from either direction
questions.explain: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing both ways; you may cross them to turn left or pass a bicyclist when safe.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Yellow Lane Lines'

questions.q: What does this single broken yellow center line mean?
options: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you may pass when it is safe
It marks the right edge of the road
Traffic moves in the same direction
questions.explain: A broken yellow line separates opposite-direction traffic; passing is allowed when safe.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Yellow Lane Lines'

questions.q: What does this broken white line mean?
options: It separates lanes going the same direction; you may change lanes when safe
questions.explain: Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes and may be crossed when safe.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'White Lane Lines'

questions.q: There are double yellow center lines; the line on YOUR side is solid and the other side is broken. May you pass?
options: Only if you are passing a truck
No, passing is not allowed from your lane
questions.explain: When the solid line is on your side, passing is not allowed (except to turn left or pass a bicyclist safely).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Yellow Lane Lines'

questions.q: What do double solid white lines between lanes mean?
options: Crossing them or changing lanes is not allowed
You may change lanes when safe
questions.explain: Double solid white lines prohibit lane changes.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'White Lane Lines'

questions.q: Which color on a traffic sign gives directional and distance guide information?
questions.explain: Green signs are guide signs for directions and distances.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Traffic Sign Colors'

questions.q: Fluorescent yellow-green signs are used to warn of:
questions.explain: Fluorescent yellow-green is used for high-emphasis school, pedestrian and bicycle warnings.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Traffic Sign Colors'

questions.q: A red X lane-use signal over a lane means:
options: You may use the lane with caution
The lane is about to close; move out soon
The lane is for turning only
questions.explain: Never drive under a red X; a yellow X means the lane signal is about to turn red.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Lane Signals'

questions.q: A drawbridge signal shows a flashing yellow light. What does it mean?
options: Speed up to cross before it opens
The bridge is in operation; slow down and prepare to stop
questions.explain: Flashing yellow at a drawbridge means it is operating; be ready to stop.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Drawbridge Signs & Signals'

questions.q: At a pedestrian hybrid beacon, the signal shows a steady red light. What must you do?
options: Stop for pedestrians in the crosswalk
Stop only if a pedestrian is on your side
Speed up before it turns flashing
questions.explain: A steady red at a pedestrian hybrid beacon means stop; flashing red means stop, then go if clear.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Pedestrian Signs & Signals'

questions.q: How close to a railroad crossing may you stop while waiting for a train or traffic?
options: Within 5 feet of the nearest rail
Not on the tracks and not within 15 feet of the crossing
Anywhere, as long as the lights are off
Directly on the tracks if the gate is up
questions.explain: Do not stop on the tracks or within 15 feet of the crossing.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Railroad Crossing Signs & Signals'

questions.q: When may you go when a traffic light turns green?
options: After waiting five seconds every time
Only after the car behind you honks
After yielding to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection
questions.explain: When the light turns green, don't move until traffic and pedestrians have cleared the intersection.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Driving Skills Test'

questions.q: When stopped at a red light, which is correct?
options: You may move into the crosswalk to see better
Do not let any part of your vehicle block the crosswalk
You may stop in the crosswalk if the light is long
Pedestrians must walk around your car
questions.explain: Never block the crosswalk or let your vehicle overhang it when stopped at a red light.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Rules for Motorists (Pedestrians)'

questions.q: When entering a 'Begin Right Turn Lane' and a bicyclist is traveling straight in that area, you must:
options: Turn in front of the bicyclist
Honk so the bicyclist moves over
Pass the bicyclist quickly on the left
questions.explain: Bicyclists traveling straight may be in the right turn lane area; drivers must yield to them.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Regulatory Signs'

questions.q: Why should you avoid driving in another vehicle's blind spot?
options: The other driver may not see you and could move into your lane
It makes your mirrors fog up
It is illegal in all cases
questions.explain: Move forward or drop back so other drivers can see you; the larger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Blind Spots'

questions.q: A law enforcement officer must complete a crash report when a crash involves:
options: Death, injury, a DUI charge, or damage that requires a vehicle to be towed
questions.explain: Officers write a report for crashes with death, injury, a DUI charge, or damage requiring towing.
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Your Responsibilities After a Crash'

questions.q: What does Florida require you to carry when driving?
options: Your driver license, plus proof of registration and insurance in the vehicle
Nothing if your information is in the state database
questions.explain: Always carry your license and have the vehicle's registration and proof of insurance with you (electronic proof of insurance is accepted).
questions.ref: Official Florida Driver License Handbook (rev. 08/2023), section 'Important Info for Minor Drivers'
